title: I've been building a steampunk idle MMORPG with AI as my coding partner — looking for playtesters and honest feedback
author: SirShaykie
selftext:
I'm a solo dev. For the past months I've been building **Chrono Tower**, a browser-based idle MMORPG with a dark steampunk / comic-anime look. You can play it now, for free, at [**https://chronotower.io**](https://chronotower.io/play?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev).

**What it is**

* **No classes.** Your weapon proficiency grows as you use the weapon. There are 8 weapon types: sword, short blade, longsword, hammer, bow, staff, steam pistol and gauntlet.
* **A 200-floor tower** across 44 biomes. Your character fights on their own. Progress continues offline for up to 8 hours.
* **7 item rarities** and 4 auto-cast skill slots. There are also 30 unique "Chrono Relic" skills that only drop from lobby bosses (meteors, black holes, time freeze, a doomsday clock…).
* **Multiplayer:** party with shared XP, PvP duels, a player market, global chat and rankings.
* **Bilingual:** English and Portuguese.

**The AI part**

All the art is drawn in code, with Canvas 2D polygons rendered through a small WebGL2 layer. There are no sprite sheets or image files.   
I use Claude Code for most of the implementation, and I design and balance the systems myself.  
The server is Node + WebSockets with an authoritative 10 Hz simulation and PostgreSQL.  
  
 I'm happy to answer questions about the workflow: what worked, what broke, and how I keep a large codebase consistent with AI help.

**What I'd love feedback on**

1. **The first 10–15 minutes.** Is it clear what to do? Where did you get confused or bored?
2. **Visual style.** Does the procedural, polygon-drawn art hold up? Does anything look off?
3. **Idle pacing.** Does progression feel rewarding, or too slow or too fast?
4. **Performance.** Tell me about lag, FPS drops or bugs, and include your device or browser.
5. **Mobile vs desktop.** If you try both, how do they compare?

Any feedback helps, even "I quit after 2 minutes because X". Bug reports are very welcome here or [https://discord.gg/PM7dN949H](https://discord.gg/PM7dN949H)

It's in beta and updated constantly, so the live game may be well ahead of the trailer.

Thanks for reading! 🙏

comments.author: zanemoore575
comments.body:
Nice work man looks interesting :)

I reckon the Ui needs a bit of simplifying though - I got met with a skill option and I was looking at the icons for a bit of a nudge on what they did, being met with a bunch of text on an ability feels like friction. I was hoping to choose get a glance at what an ability does in simple terms so I could select but I just couldn’t even figure out what to choose even reading them. 

Be cool to see you make some real in game art icons for the abilities etc too! The SVGs or draw an icons are definitely letting it down. 

I only played for a few minutes to check it out but did feel like my character kind of just circled around one area, I didn’t think I could control the character to choose the path and I was hoping I would go down a more lineal path automatically rather than just wander around.

That’s just me though!   
Keep going 💪

replies.author: SirShaykie
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for the feedback, I’ll get to work on that right away!!
Did you test it on PC or mobile?
